conviction_note: Aiming publishes no full-year plan, only a forecast for the next quarter, so this print gives the first FY2026 number, which implies a Q4 guide. The Q3 operating-profit beat on its own guide (482m) is routine: it has beaten six quarters in a row and the stock still fell 7.7%, 7.9% and 9.8% after three of the last four prints. The lean is mildly negative, based on inference that the Q4 guide will carry the launch cost of hololive mahjong (influencer pre-play 12-20 Nov) on top of Inazuma decay, after a +25% hololive-driven run from 167 to 208. abs_move 7 sits above the 5.95 proxy because a new guide comes with this release, and p_up 44 because this is inference, not a document; findings sum -0.95 against a scaled -0.84.
bar: Company's own Jan-Sep 2026 forecast published 2026-07-29 (Q2 tanshin, percentages corrected 2026-08-03): sales 11,351m, OP 1,012m, ordinary 682m, NP 622m. The Q3 standalone figures are sales 4,479m, OP 482m, ordinary 324m, NP 239m. Sources: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260729501676.pdf ; https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260729501731.pdf (p.23) ; https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260803/140120260803507049.pdf. No analyst consensus exists (kabuyoho consensus page blank: https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=3911). The FY/Q4 number has no bar at all. print_vs_bar_pct is on cumulative OP and assumes a Q3 OP of about 560m, in line with the beat record.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register as of 2026-10-26: 3.69% of shares across 2 disclosed sellers, -0.02pt change (flat, neither building nor covering) (https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html, via baseline). kabutan lists 3911 as a buy-only 制度信用 name (not 貸借), so there are no margin shorts and the 信用倍率 is undefined (kabutan shows '－'); the margin balance page sits behind a captcha. There is no option market and no skew. The 20-day run-up is +18.9%, nearly all of it from the 2026-10-09 hololive mahjong announcement (+16.8% on 9.75m shares against a ~0.15m norm); 5-day -2.8%. A 3.7% disclosed short against a negative is not crowded enough to squeeze on its own, but it does make a positive guide surprise more explosive.

findings.finding: This release carries the first FY2026 forecast (Aiming only guides the next quarter). Q4 will absorb the launch of 'ホロライブ麻雀' (influencer pre-play 12-20 Nov 2026, launch '2026', so late Nov/Dec) on top of the Inazuma Eleven Cross decay management has already flagged. The Q4 guide is therefore likely weak against holders who bought the hololive news. Precedent: at Q3 2025 the FY guide implied a Q4 operating loss (FY OP 1,935 against 9M actual 2,098) and the stock fell about 7.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reactions follow the next-period guide, not the beat. Q3'25: beat on OP, Q4 loss implied, about -7.7%. Q1'26: weak H1 guide, -7.9%. Q2'26: Q2 OP beat its guide by 61% and Q3 guided OP +67% QoQ, yet the stock went 205 to 185 (-9.8%, Yahoo daily bars 2026-07-29/30; kabutan 7/30 '急落'). Q4'25: +1.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: No Q4 or FY number exists: Aiming publishes no full-year plan and there is no analyst consensus (kabuyoho consensus blank), so nobody can hold a bar for Q4. Since 10/09 the price has added about ¥41 (+25%) on the hololive pipeline without any cost line attached. If the launch cost were priced, the stock would not have held 208-216 after the announcement spike; it would have given back toward 170-180 as it did after the Inazuma launch hype in July.
findings.independence: Management's own H2 decay assumption for Inazuma ('下期は逓減想定', CEO at the Q2 briefing, https://gamebiz.jp/news/430206, 2026-07-29) is a separate source pointing the same way. Weakens it: the 2026-10-19 Kage-jitsu Thai/Vietnam licence, whose post-October effect the company says will sit inside the next guide (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261019/140120261019552790.pdf).

findings.finding: Aiming has beaten its own quarterly operating-profit guide in each of the last six periods (Q1'25 +15.6%, H1'25 +25.5%, 9M'25 +14.4%, FY'25 2,079 vs 1,935, Q1'26 +86%, H1'26 +61.5%), mostly through cost control (outsourcing, platform fees), so a Q3 OP above the 482m standalone guide is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold three times in the last four prints (see guidance finding). The beat only paid in Q1'25 and Q2'25 (+25%, +21%), when it came with a profit turnaround.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the beat pattern is visible in every 差異 notice, so it is sized small. What is not priced is its size this quarter, because Q3 is the first full quarter of Inazuma ad and royalty costs.
findings.independence: The earlier variance notices are separate documents: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251028/140120251028580145.pdf (9M'25), https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260428/140120260428513188.pdf (Q1'26).

findings.finding: Inazuma Eleven Cross, the new title behind the Q3 guide's +857m QoQ sales step, ranked #25 in Sensor Tower's June monthly chart with three weeks live, but is absent from the July monthly top 30 and the 22-28 August weekly App Store top 30. Q3 sales may fall short of 4,479m, as Q1'26 sales missed by 4.7%, while operating profit is protected by costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26 sales missed the guide by 4.7% while OP beat by 86%, and the stock fell 7.9%. Not separable from that print's weak H1 guide.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (July 2026 monthly ranking; page shows Sensor Tower table, Inazuma absent from top 30)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the charts are public, and the guide already assumed decay. What remains is the gap between a 'decay' assumption and dropping out of the top 30 within a month. A priced sales miss would show as a stock that never recovered after the 7/30 fall, which is what happened (172-186 through Aug-Sep) until the hololive news.
findings.independence: Weekly ranking https://gamebiz.jp/news/431884 (2026-08-29; 22-28 Aug, Inazuma absent from top 30), same vendor. Against it: CEO said July remained strong (https://gamebiz.jp/news/430206), and the title re-entered the App Store top 20 on 2026-10-14 (https://gamebiz.jp/news/433996).

findings.finding: Q4 demand signals are better than Q3's: Inazuma Eleven Cross re-entered the App Store sales top 20 (#16) on 2026-10-14 with the Shin Aphrodi pick-up gacha. On 2026-10-19 Aiming signed an exclusive Thai/Vietnam licence for Kage-jitsu Master of Garden with Razer Game Services, and the company says the post-October effect goes into the next forecast. Either could lift the Q4 guide above a pure launch-cost quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The Q2'26 guide stepped up 67% QoQ in OP and was still sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The licence drew a 'limited' reaction (kabutan/Fisco 10/20: 反落), and a one-day top-20 re-entry is not in any number the market holds. A priced version would show a move on 10/14 or 10/19; 10/14 closed -3.8% and 10/19 +2.9% with the Standard-market news.
findings.independence: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261019/140120261019552790.pdf (company licence notice, 2026-10-19). It is a different document from the ranking source.

outside_window.finding: Kage-jitsu console game 'Phantom Echoes' (PS5/Switch 2/Steam) ships in 2027, so it adds no revenue this year. The dividend decision comes in December (2025's came on 12/16 and was 無配), so no capital return lands with this print.

baseline_tension: The baseline's priced lean is +1.31, driven by a 3.69% disclosed short (squeeze component +2.21), and my net is mildly negative, so I cut against the lean but agree with the run-up component (-0.94). The strongest positive the release could carry is a Q4 guide that books the hololive launch and the Kage-jitsu licence as revenue rather than cost, on top of the routine OP beat. I looked for it, and the October Inazuma top-20 re-entry and the licence are filed as a +0.5 finding. No buyback or dividend is expected at this print.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a public series): the Inazuma ranking finding uses public Sensor Tower and gamebiz charts the market already has, so I cut it from -0.5 to -0.25 and moved p_up from 42 to 44.

Rule 2 (check the sign): two negatives and two positives; I wrote the strongest positive into baseline_tension and confirmed no capital return is due at this print. The guidance finding stays at -1.5 because it rests on what the release ADDS (the first FY number), not on a visible miss.
Open question 4 (a run-in is not a short signal): I did not file the +18.9% run-up as a finding; it enters only as context in why_not_priced.
